title: Circuit policy parameter sweep and tenant impact simulator
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a reproducible parameter-sweep harness and visualizer to evaluate different circuit-breaker and load-shedding policy parameters against tenant workloads across regions. The goal is to map policy parameter space (latency thresholds, error-rate windows, admit-score cutoffs, hysteresis) to tenant-level outcomes (p95/p99 latency, error budget burn, admitted request fraction), and expose those mappings in a Grafana-style dashboard so SREs and PMs can choose safe defaults and per-tenant overrides.
context: We already have regional SLOs and token-level SLIs (token.p95_ms, token.p99_ms, token.kv_hit, token.decode_ms) instrumented across the stack. However, configuration decisions for admission/circuit policies are currently manual and rely on anecdotal runs. This ticket creates a systematic way to (1) sweep parameters, (2) run synthetic and sampled production-like traces, (3) capture per-tenant impact and failover ripple across regions, and (4) present results for policy selection and rollout playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Parameter-sweep harness that runs N=20 sweeps in parallel against configurable synthetic workloads
Simulator outputs per-run CSV with metrics: tenant_id, region, admitted_fraction, p95_ms, p99_ms, error_rate, kv_hit_rate, avg_tokens_per_req
Grafana dashboard with heatmaps + linked run details for every parameter combination
Playbook section that recommends safe parameter ranges for hosted vs dedicated customers
Feature-flag gated rollout for the new admission policy controller with automatic rollback on regression
implementation_notes: Harness implemented as a Go service (sim-sweeper) that uses the existing synthetic traffic generator (simgen) and the admissions API stub. It should be able to re-play sampled prefix distributions from the sampling pipeline (bucketed by tenant cohort). Metrics are pushed to the test Prometheus instance and tagged with sweep.id and run.id. Avoid modifying prod metrics streams; use test namespaces and labels.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use sampled production prefix distributions for realism vs fully synthetic sequences to cover edge cases. Tradeoff: sampling increases complexity but yields higher fidelity results.
Parameter sweep is grid-based initially; avoid full Bayesian optimization for first iteration to keep results explainable to PMs/ops.
Run in a regional staging environment to capture KV cache/serve-runtime effects. Tradeoff: staging hardware differs from prod, so absolute numbers will need normalization factors in the dashboard.
observability_spec: Metrics emitted per-sweep: sweep.id, run.id, tenant.id, region, param.latency_threshold_ms, param.error_window_s, param.admit_cutoff, admitted_count, total_count, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, decode_ms, kv_hit_rate, error_rate, fallback_rate, region_fanout_count. Create Grafana panels: 1) parameter-space heatmap (admitted_fraction vs latency_threshold x admit_cutoff), 2) per-tenant violin plots of p95 across runs, 3) failover ripple timeline showing downstream region traffic shifts, 4) cost estimator (token/sec * estimated unit-cost).
risks: Simulator results may diverge from prod due to hardware and traffic shaping differences; must annotate dashboard with confidence bands.
Large sweeps can produce high load in staging clusters; need enforced quotas and safety kill-switch.
Per-tenant regressions could be masked when aggregating; ensure per-tenant breakdown is available and browsable.
runbook_playbook_notes: When a parameter set causes >10% admitted drop for any paying tenant, abort rollout and notify Customer Success and Eng on-call
For hosted customers, default to conservative admit_cutoff=0.65 and latency_threshold_ms=1200; for dedicated tiers allow a tighter admit_cutoff=0.8 if p99 latency remains within SLOs
If KV hit rate drops below baseline by >8% during experiment, mark run unstable and exclude from comparisons
